intro_html: Gochujang gives these Korean ground beef bowls a deep, savory heat that tastes like you fussed for hours. Lean beef browns and simmers in a spicy sweet sauce, then goes over rice with broccoli. It runs a bit higher at around $4.69 a serving (at everyday cost), but you still get a big 50 grams of protein across 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $4.69 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl brings 50 grams of protein and 615 calories across all 14 servings.
upsell_html: One tub of gochujang unlocks a whole world of cheap, punchy dinners, and this is a great place to start. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A tub of gochujang seasons batch after batch. Buy one tub of gochujang and it will carry you through months of meals.
Sesame oil is strong, so a little goes a long way. One small bottle of sesame oil lasts a very long time.
Lean ground beef is the big cost here. Watch for ground beef sales and buy extra to freeze when the price is right.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it apart, then drain the grease.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, and brown sugar and stir into a glossy sauce.
Toss in the broccoli florets and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet simmers.
Pile the beef and broccoli over the rice and serve.
